# roost

> `top` for Claude Code: a terminal dashboard for every live Claude Code session on a
> machine — the model each one is on, how much context window it has burned, whether it
> is working, idle, or stuck waiting for input — and, unlike any other tool in this space,
> the subagents each session has spawned underneath it.

Single-file, dependency-free Python 3.9+ program. Runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows.
Read-only: it inspects local Claude Code session state and never modifies a session,
a working tree, or a git repository.

## What it's for

Anyone running several Claude Code sessions at once — across multiple projects,
worktrees, or machines — loses track of which ones need attention. roost groups
sessions by how costly they are to ignore: sessions near their context limit surface
first, sessions parked mid-task with a large context bill next, then everything
actively working, then quiet sessions collapse into a single line. It also surfaces
subagents spawned by a session (background Task/Agent calls), which is otherwise
invisible from outside that session.

## Install

- Homebrew (macOS/Linux): `brew install gmhoward9289-ops/tap/roost`
- Debian/Ubuntu (apt, with upgrade support): see README
- npm: `npm install -g roost-top` (note: the package name on npm is `roost-top`,
  not `roost` — the bare name `roost` on the npm registry belongs to an unrelated
  "system provisioning toolkit" package)
- Direct download: GitHub Releases

  to roost's focus on model/context/subagent state.
